skill.name: lean-build
skill.description: Build feature work with high overbuilding risk. Use for new behavior, product slices, or integrations where repository reuse, strict scope, and an explicit stop condition matter.
skill.summary: Deliver the smallest coherent feature slice that meets observable acceptance criteria.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: No security findings were identified in the prompt-only skill. It contains implementation guidance without executable code, external access, data collection, or prompt injection.

content.value_statement: Feature work often grows beyond acceptance needs and weakens architectural ownership. Lean Build defines a narrow outcome, reuses repository patterns, and stops after focused verification.
actual_capabilities: Derives observable acceptance criteria and explicit non-goals from the request and repository.
Traces the feature entry point through layers that own relevant invariants.
Selects existing repository patterns and ownership boundaries for implementation.
Guides a coherent feature path across every responsible layer.
Identifies when focused refactoring is necessary to avoid duplication or weakened ownership.
Stops implementation after acceptance passes and reports material omissions.
limitations: Requires clear repository context and a feature request to derive reliable acceptance criteria.
Does not replace comprehensive security, performance, or release review.
Does not add optional modes, providers, configuration, or polish unless acceptance requires them.
Provides workflow guidance but does not guarantee that repository tests cover every regression.

use_cases.title: Deliver a Product Slice
use_cases.description: Implement one observable user outcome across the repository while excluding unrelated enhancements.

use_cases.title: Constrain an Integration
use_cases.description: Add a required integration using existing ownership boundaries and only necessary lifecycle changes.

use_cases.title: Correct Shared Behavior
use_cases.description: Fix a narrow behavior at its owning layer and verify the affected path.

prompt_templates.title: Define the Smallest Outcome
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $lean-build to implement [feature]. First state observable acceptance criteria and explicit non-goals from this repository.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a clear feature goal

prompt_templates.title: Reuse Repository Ownership
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $lean-build for [feature]. Trace the entry point and owning layers, then implement the smallest coherent path using existing patterns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Feature work spanning known repository layers

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Focused Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $lean-build to add [behavior]. Refactor only where direct patching would duplicate behavior, weaken ownership, or hide the root cause.
prompt_templates.scenario: Existing architecture makes a local patch risky

prompt_templates.title: Deliver a Constrained Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $lean-build to integrate [service]. Define lifecycle needs, material tradeoffs, focused verification, and the exact stop condition before implementation.

output_examples.input: Add saved filters to the issue list without introducing new configuration.
output_examples.output: Acceptance covers saving, selecting, and deleting filters through existing preference ownership. Non-goals exclude sharing, import, export, and filter templates.

output_examples.input: Connect the current notification flow to a second provider.
output: Trace the existing notification entry point, provider boundary, retry ownership, and test path.
Add only the provider implementation and required registration.
Stop after focused delivery and failure-path checks pass.

output_examples.input: Fix duplicate status updates appearing in two interface views.
output_examples.output: Move deduplication to the shared status owner, preserve both views, and verify the common update path plus focused regression coverage.

best_practices: Provide the feature request, repository context, and expected user-visible result.
Confirm acceptance criteria and non-goals before implementation begins.
Run focused tests on the complete path and stop when acceptance passes.
anti_patterns: Do not add extensibility, providers, modes, or configuration for hypothetical future needs.
Do not force cross-layer behavior into one local patch when ownership belongs elsewhere.
Do not continue polishing after acceptance passes without a new requirement.

faq.question: What types of work fit Lean Build?
faq.answer: It fits new behavior, product slices, integrations, and narrow fixes where scope growth is a concern.

faq.question: Does the skill always choose the fewest changed files?
faq.answer: No. It favors the smallest coherent outcome across responsible layers, which may require several focused changes.

faq.question: When does it recommend refactoring?
faq.answer: It recommends refactoring when a direct patch duplicates behavior, weakens ownership, or hides the root cause.

faq.question: Will it add configuration for future flexibility?
faq.answer: Only when acceptance or lifecycle design requires configuration. Speculative options remain out of scope.

faq.question: How does it decide when to stop?
faq.answer: It stops when the observable acceptance path passes focused verification and only material omissions remain.

faq.question: Does Lean Build replace broader testing?
faq.answer: No. It emphasizes focused proof for the changed path, while broader validation remains a repository and release responsibility.
